_comment: Hand-verified replacements for learning outcomes whose PDF layout (stacked fractions, tables, super/subscript notation) cannot be linearised automatically. Keys are <unitCode>:<loId>. 'text' replaces the stem, 'bullets' replaces individual bullets by index, 'tier' forces the tier, 'table' attaches structured table data. The automatic text is preserved as autoText for auditing.

B1:1.3.1.note: Reagent colour-change table (spec p.13) linearised by hand; structured copy in 'table'.
B1:1.3.1.text: recall the following reagents and their colour changes: Benedict’s – initial colour blue, end colour for positive result brick red precipitate; iodine solution – initial colour yellow–brown, end colour blue–black; Biuret – initial colour blue, end colour lilac/purple; ethanol – initial colour colourless, end colour white emulsion

C2:2.6.7.note: Atom economy fraction (spec p.64) set as a stacked fraction multiplied by 100.
C2:2.6.7.text: calculate the atom economy of a reaction to form a desired product from the balanced equation: (mass of desired product / total mass of products) × 100

P1:1.1.3.note: First bullet has two side-by-side stacked fractions (spec p.70): average velocity = displacement/time and v = d/t.

bullets.0: displacement, time and average velocity: average velocity = displacement / time; v = d / t

P1:1.4.17.note: Kinetic energy equation (spec p.79) is set with a stacked ½ and a superscript 2.
P1:1.4.17.text: explain that kinetic energy Ek is the energy possessed by a moving object and recall and use the equation Ek = ½mv² to calculate kinetic energy in joules, where m is the mass of the object in kg and v is the speed of the object in m/s.

P1:1.5.3.note: Nuclide notation (spec p.81): mass number A as a superscript and atomic number Z as a subscript before the element symbol; written here as [A,Z]X.
P1:1.5.3.text: describe a nucleus in terms of atomic number Z and mass number A, using the notation [A,Z]X (mass number A written as a superscript and atomic number Z as a subscript before the element symbol X);

P1:1.5.7.note: Decay equations (spec p.81) use superscript/subscript nuclide notation; written here as [mass number, atomic number]Symbol. The whole outcome is set in bold (Higher Tier).
P1:1.5.7.text: describe nuclear disintegrations in terms of equations involving mass numbers and atomic numbers, and complete the equations by balancing the mass numbers and atomic numbers: alpha decay: [A,Z]X → [A−4,Z−2]Y + [4,2]He (or [4,2]α); beta decay: [A,Z]X → [A,Z+1]Y + [0,−1]e (or [0,−1]β); gamma decay: [A,Z]X → [A,Z]X + γ
